headline: Analog Devices drops 17% as a flat first-quarter outlook meets a chip sell-off
summary: Analog Devices fell 17.4% to $312.95 after record fourth-quarter results, with revenue up 42% to $4.37 billion. Its first-quarter forecast of $4.4 billion revenue and $3.82 adjusted earnings per share implies a flat quarter after a steep recovery, on a day when chip stocks fell sharply.
why: The quarter itself was very strong: gross margin rose to 69.3%, operating margin to 42.7% and adjusted earnings per share 80% to $4.06, and full-year free cash flow reached $5.5 billion. The guidance disappointed because revenue is expected to be roughly flat and adjusted earnings per share lower in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, a sign that the sharpest part of the analog chip recovery may be over.

The timing made it worse: the report came on a day when semiconductor stocks fell hard after Monday’s rally, so investors sold any chipmaker that gave them a reason to. Management stressed that more than two-thirds of its growth came from markets not centred on AI.
context: On November 24 the Nasdaq fell about 1.5% and the S&P 500 about 0.5% while the Dow rose almost 0.9%, as chip stocks gave back much of the previous day’s rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. Nvidia fell about 6–7% and AMD, Micron and Broadcom also dropped.
Money rotated out of semiconductors and AI hardware into health care, consumer staples and retailers, so most stocks rose even as the technology-heavy indexes fell.
